stem:
Kabir examines a rock with several different minerals visible. He also studies a native mineral that is a pure element, and another mineral made of more than one element.

Which claims classify these materials correctly? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: The rock is a mixture of minerals.
The native mineral that is a pure element is not a compound.
The mineral made of more than one element is still an element.
The rock is a compound because several minerals sit together in one solid piece.

teacher.key_rationale: Rocks are mixtures of minerals; a native pure-element mineral is not a compound. Calling a multi-element mineral an element, or treating a solid rock piece as a compound, miss that classification hinge.
